tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

- 不要弹 Windows 通知；完成后 send_message 给 lead：摘要 + 实测 + 两张截图路径 + 结论。

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

{"tasks":[{"id":"task-19","revision":1,"subject":"备战界面：装备悬停信息（简略/详细切换）+ 拖动调序","description":"目标：备战界面（scenes/loadout.tscn + scripts/ui/LoadoutScreen.gd，你自己上次写的）加两项交互：装备悬停信息（详细/简略可切换）+ 拖动调整 6 个装备槽顺序。只改 scripts/ui/LoadoutScreen.gd（如需也仅限该文件）。

一、悬停装备信息浮层
- 鼠标停在「装备库」装备卡或「当前方案」装备槽上 0.15s 内弹出信息浮层（PanelContainer，约 460×可变高，UiKit.skin_card，z_index 高、mouse_filter IGNORE），跟随鼠标 +18px 并自动 clamp 在 2400×1400 内（贴近右/下边缘时翻到左侧/上方）。
- 两种模式，顶栏（或装备库标题行右侧）放一个分段切换按钮「简略 / 详细」，选中态金色，切换立即影响后续浮层（已弹出的可即时刷新），默认「简略」。
- 简略：装备名（金）+ 价格 + 一级/二级/三级/终极（tier 中文：小件/中件/大件/终极）+ 该装备 2~3 条主要属性（攻击/法强/护甲/魔抗/生命/法力/攻速/暴击/吸血/冷却等，只列非零项，取前 3 条）。
- 详细：名称/价格/分类/tier + 全部非零属性逐行（格式「攻击 +75」）+ 「被动/主动」描述（item["passive"]/item["active"] 有则显示）+ 「合成来源」（item["requires"] 列组件名 + 合计价，无则显示「基础装备」）。
- 移出卡片/移动时更新位置，移出即隐藏；占位或空槽不弹。

二、拖动调整出装顺序
- 「当前方案」6 个装备槽支持拖拽交换：实现 Godot 拖放 API（`_get_drag_data` 返回 {"from_slot": i}，`_can_drop_data` 目标槽有效且携带 from_slot，`_drop_data` 交换两槽 `_slot_ids` 后刷新），拖动时用 `set_drag_preview` 显示一个装备名小卡。

2) windowed 探针加载 loadout.tscn：给 6 槽填 3 件后调用 `_swap_slots(0, 2)` 打印 `_slot_ids` 变化；构造 InputEventMouseMotion 或直接调用你的 hover 显示函数（如 `_show_item_tip("battle_axe", pos)`）截图 screenshots/loadout_tip_detail.png（详细模式）与 loadout_tip_simple.png（简略模式）；打印浮层 rect 在屏内；日志 0 SCRIPT ERROR/Invalid call/Nonexistent。

一、悬停装备信息浮层
- 鼠标停在「装备库」装备卡或「当前方案」装备槽上 0.15s 内弹出信息浮层（PanelContainer，约 460×可变高，UiKit.skin_card，z_index 高、mouse_filter IGNORE），跟随鼠标 +18px 并自动 clamp 在 2400×1400 内（贴近右/下边缘时翻到左侧/上方）。
- 两种模式，顶栏（或装备库标题行右侧）放一个分段切换按钮「简略 / 详细」，选中态金色，切换立即影响后续浮层（已弹出的可即时刷新），默认「简略」。
- 简略：装备名（金）+ 价格 + 一级/二级/三级/终极（tier 中文：小件/中件/大件/终极）+ 该装备 2~3 条主要属性（攻击/法强/护甲/魔抗/生命/法力/攻速/暴击/吸血/冷却等，只列非零项，取前 3 条）。

- 移出卡片/移动时更新位置，移出即隐藏；占位或空槽不弹。

```
class SlotButton extends Button:
	var slot_index := 0
	var item_id := ""
	var screen: LoadoutScreen
	func _get_drag_data(_at_position: Vector2) -> Variant:
		if item_id == "":
			return null
		var p := PanelContainer.new()  # preview card

`UiKit.flat` accessible inside inner class via autoload; ItemDatabase too.

- `_drop_data`: `if data is Dictionary and data.has("from_slot"): screen._swap_slots(int(data["from_slot"]), slot_index)`.

```
func _swap_slots(a: int, b: int) -> void:
	if a < 0 or b < 0 or a >= SLOT_COUNT or b >= SLOT_COUNT or a == b:
		return
	var tmp := str(_slot_ids[a])
	_slot_ids[a] = str(_slot_ids[b])

On × button handle drag? × is a Button with mouse filter STOP; pressing it won't start parent drag. Fine.

一、悬停装备信息浮层
- 鼠标停在「装备库」装备卡或「当前方案」装备槽上 0.15s 内弹出信息浮层（PanelContainer，约 460×可变高，UiKit.skin_card，z_index 高、mouse_filter IGNORE），跟随鼠标 +18px 并自动 clamp 在 2400×1400 内（贴近右/下边缘时翻到左侧/上方）。
- 两种模式，顶栏（或装备库标题行右侧）放一个分段切换按钮「简略 / 详细」，选中态金色，切换立即影响后续浮层（已弹出的可即时刷新），默认「简略」。
- 简略：装备名（金）+ 价格 + 一级/二级/三级/终极（tier 中文：小件/中件/大件/终极）+ 该装备 2~3 条主要属性（攻击/法强/护甲/魔抗/生命/法力/攻速/暴击/吸血/冷却等，只列非零项，取前 3 条）。
- 详细：名称/价格/分类/tier + 全部非零属性逐行（格式「攻击 +75」）+ 「被动/主动」描述（item["passive"]/item["active"] 有则显示）+ 「合成来源」（item["requires"] 列组件名 + 合计价，无则显示「基础装备」）。
- 移出卡片/移动时更新位置，移出即隐藏；占位或空槽不弹。

- 「当前方案」6 个装备槽支持拖拽交换：实现 Godot 拖放 API（`_get_drag_data` 返回 {"from_slot": i}，`_can_drop_data` 目标槽有效且携带 from_slot，`_drop_data` 交换两槽 `_slot_ids` 后刷新），拖动时用 `set_drag_preview` 显示一个装备名小卡。

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt one teammate's current turn while preserving its pending inbox. Team Lead only.

target.description: Teammate target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the Lead and every durable teammate with an addressable target and current availability. inactive means no turn is executing, not a task result. provisioning and failed describe member creation.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

</system-reminder>

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

func _place_tip(pos: Vector2) -> void:
	if _tip == null or not _tip.visible:
		return
	var sz := _tip.size
	var p := pos + Vector2(18, 18)
	if p.x + sz.x > UiKit.DESIGN_W - 8.0:
		p.x = pos.x - sz.x - 18.0
	if p.y + sz.y > UiKit.DESIGN_H - 8.0:
		p.y = pos.y - sz.y - 18.0
	p.x = clampf(p.x, 8.0, UiKit.DESIGN_W - sz.x - 8.0)
	p.y = clampf(p.y, 8.0, UiKit.DESIGN_H - sz.y - 8.0)
	_tip.position = p

func _place_tip(pos: Vector2) -> void:
	if _tip == null or not _tip.visible:
		return
	var sz := _tip.size
	var p := pos + Vector2(18, 18)
	if p.x + sz.x > UiKit.DESIGN_W - 8.0:
		p.x = pos.x - sz.x - 18.0
	if p.y + sz.y > UiKit.DESIGN_H - 8.0:
		p.y = pos.y - sz.y - 18.0
	p.x = clampf(p.x, 8.0, UiKit.DESIGN_W - sz.x - 8.0)
	p.y = clampf(p.y, 8.0, UiKit.DESIGN_H - sz.y - 8.0)
	_tip.position = p

{"content":"extends Control
## 临时探针（跑完删除）：备战界面悬停浮层（简略/详细）+ 拖动调序 + 存档回归。

var _screen: Control
var _res_backup := ""
var _res_existed := false
var _user_existed := false


func _ready() -> void:
	_res_existed = FileAccess.file_exists("res://saves/hero_builds.json")
	if _res_existed:
		_res_backup = FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://saves/hero_builds.json")
	_user_existed = FileAccess.file_exists("user://hero_builds.json")
	var ps: Control = load("res://scenes/loadout.tscn").instantiate()
	add_child(ps)
	_screen = ps
	await _frames(4)
	print("PROBE_READY hero=", _screen._hero_name, " tip_filter=", _screen._tip.mouse_filter,
		" mode=", _screen._tip_mode)

	# 填 3 件（妲己 / 物理）
	_screen._hero_btns["妲己"].pressed.emit()
	await _frames(2)
	var ids: Array = _screen._item_ids_by_cat.get("物理", [])
	for i in range(3):
		_screen._item_btns[str(ids[i])].pressed.emit()
		await _frames(1)
	print("PROBE_SLOTS=", _screen._slot_ids)
	_screen._name_edit.text = "测试流"
	_screen._save_btn.pressed.emit()
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_BUILDS_妲己=", HeroBuildStore.get_builds("妲己"))

	# 切换英雄再切回 → 自动载入
	_screen._hero_btns["吕布"].pressed.emit()
	await _frames(2)
	_screen._hero_btns["妲己"].pressed.emit()
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_RELOAD=", _screen._slot_ids)

	# 拖拽调序：_swap_slots(0, 2)
	var before: Array = _screen._slot_ids.duplicate()
	_screen._swap_slots(0, 2)
	await _frames(2)
	print("PROBE_SWAP_BEFORE=", before, " AFTER=", _screen._slot_ids,
		" toast=", _screen._toast.visible, " ", _screen._toast_lab.text)

	# 拖放 API 直测（_can_drop_data / _drop_data 内部走 _swap_slots）
	var payload := {"from_slot": 0}
	var target: Control = _screen._slot_btns[2]
	print("PROBE_DRAG_CAN_DROP=", target._can_drop_data(Vector2.ZERO, payload),
		" bad_data=", target._can_drop_data(Vector2.ZERO, {}))
	target._drop_data(Vector2.ZERO, payload)
	await _frames(2)
	print("PROBE_DROP_SLOTS=", _screen._slot_ids)

	# 悬停浮层：简略
	_screen._on_tip_mode("simple")
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(1180, 690))
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_TIP_SIMPLE visible=", _screen._tip.visible, " rect=", _screen._tip.get_global_rect(),
		" size=", _screen._tip.size, " mode=", _screen._tip_mode)
	await _frames(2)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img1 := get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()
	print("PROBE_SHOT_SIMPLE=", img1.save_png("res://screenshots/loadout_tip_simple.png"))

	# 悬停浮层：详细
	_screen._on_tip_mode("detail")
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(1180, 690))
	await _frames(3)
	var detail_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_DETAIL visible=", _screen._tip.visible, " rect=", detail_rect,
		" size=", _screen._tip.size, " mode=", _screen._tip_mode)
	await _frames(2)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img2 := get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()
	print("PROBE_SHOT_DETAIL=", img2.save_png("res://screenshots/loadout_tip_detail.png"))

	# 贴边翻转 / clamp：右下角触发
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(2380, 1390))
	await _frames(2)
	var edge_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_EDGE rect=", edge_rect, " in_screen=",
		edge_rect.position.x >= 0.0 and edge_rect.position.y >= 0.0
		and edge_rect.end.x <= 2400.0 and edge_rect.end.y <= 1400.0)
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(30, 30))
	await _frames(2)
	var top_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_TOPLEFT rect=", top_rect, " in_screen=",
		top_rect.position.x >= 0.0 and top_rect.position.y >= 0.0
		and top_rect.end.x <= 2400.0 and top_rect.end.y <= 1400.0)
	_screen._hide_tip()
	await _frames(1)
	print("PROBE_TIP_HIDDEN=", _screen._tip.visible)

	# 方案删除 + 返回按钮
	for a in _screen._build_actions:
		if str(a.get("name", "")) == "测试流":
			a["del"].pressed.emit()
			break
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_AFTER_DELETE=", HeroBuildStore.get_builds("妲己"))
	print("PROBE_RETURN_BTN=", _screen._return_btn != null and _screen._return_btn.visible,
		" text=", _screen._return_btn.text)

	_restore()
	await _frames(2)
	get_tree().quit()


func _frames(n: int) -> void:
	for i in range(n):
		await get_tree().process_frame


func _restore() -> void:
	if not _user_existed:
		DirAccess.remove_absolute("user://hero_builds.json")
	if _res_existed:
		var f := FileAccess.open("res://saves/hero_builds.json", FileAccess.WRITE)
		if f != null:
			f.store_string(_res_backup)
			f.close()
","file_path":"scripts/ui/_LoadoutProbe.gd"}

	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw

	await _frames(2)
	var edge_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_EDGE rect=", edge_rect, " in_screen=",
		edge_rect.position.x >= 0.0 and edge_rect.position.y >= 0.0
		and edge_rect.end.x <= 2400.0 and edge_rect.end.y <= 1400.0)
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(30, 30))
	await _frames(2)
	var top_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_TOPLEFT rect=", top_rect, " in_screen=",
		top_rect.position.x >= 0.0 and top_rect.position.y >= 0.0
		and top_rect.end.x <= 2400.0 and top_rect.end.y <= 1400.0)
	_screen._on_tip_mode("simple")
	await _frames(2)
	print("PROBE_TIP_LIVE_SWITCH visible=", _screen._tip.visible, " size=", _screen._tip.size,
		" mode=", _screen._tip_mode)
	_screen._hide_tip()
	await _frames(1)
	print("PROBE_TIP_HIDDEN=", _screen._tip.visible)

	for a in _screen._build_actions:
		if str(a.get("name", "")) == "测试流":
			a["del"].pressed.emit()
			break
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_AFTER_DELETE=", HeroBuildStore.get_builds("妲己"))
	print("PROBE_RETURN_BTN=", _screen._return_btn != null and _screen._return_btn.visible,
		" text=", _screen._return_btn.text)

	_restore()
	await _frames(2)
	get_tree().quit()


func _frames(n: int) -> void:
	for i in range(n):

	if not _user_existed:

	if _res_existed:
		var f := FileAccess.open("res://saves/hero_builds.json", FileAccess.WRITE)
		if f != null:

var _user_existed := false

		" mode=", _screen._tip_mode)

	_screen._hero_btns["妲己"].pressed.emit()
	await _frames(2)
	var ids: Array = _screen._item_ids_by_cat.get("物理", [])
	for i in range(3):
		_screen._item_btns[str(ids[i])].pressed.emit()
		await _frames(1)
	print("PROBE_SLOTS=", _screen._slot_ids)
	_screen._name_edit.text = "测试流"
	_screen._save_btn.pressed.emit()
	await _frames(3)

	_screen._hero_btns["吕布"].pressed.emit()
	await _frames(2)
	_screen._hero_btns["妲己"].pressed.emit()
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_RELOAD=", _screen._slot_ids)

	var before: Array = _screen._slot_ids.duplicate()
	_screen._swap_slots(0, 2)
	await _frames(2)
	print("PROBE_SWAP_BEFORE=", before, " AFTER=", _screen._slot_ids,
		" toast=", _screen._toast.visible, " ", _screen._toast_lab.text)

	var payload := {"from_slot": 0}
	var target: Control = _screen._slot_btns[2]
	print("PROBE_DRAG_CAN_DROP=", target._can_drop_data(Vector2.ZERO, payload),
		" bad_data=", target._can_drop_data(Vector2.ZERO, {}))
	target._drop_data(Vector2.ZERO, payload)
	await _frames(2)
	print("PROBE_DROP_SLOTS=", _screen._slot_ids)

	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(1180, 690))
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_TIP_SIMPLE visible=", _screen._tip.visible, " rect=", _screen._tip.get_global_rect(),
		" size=", _screen._tip.size, " mode=", _screen._tip_mode)
	await _frames(2)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img1 := get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()
	print("PROBE_SHOT_SIMPLE=", img1.save_png("res://screenshots/loadout_tip_simple.png"))

	_screen._on_tip_mode("detail")
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(1180, 690))
	await _frames(3)
	var detail_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_DETAIL visible=", _screen._tip.visible, " rect=", detail_rect,
		" size=", _screen._tip.size, " mode=", _screen._tip_mode)
	await _frames(2)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img2 := get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()
	print("PROBE_SHOT_DETAIL=", img2.save_png("res://screenshots/loadout_tip_detail.png"))

	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(2380, 1390))
	await _frames(2)
	var edge_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_EDGE rect=", edge_rect, " in_screen=",
		edge_rect.position.x >= 0.0 and edge_rect.position.y >= 0.0
		and edge_rect.end.x <= 2400.0 and edge_rect.end.y <= 1400.0)
	_screen._show_item_tip("battle_axe", Vector2(30, 30))
	await _frames(2)
	var top_rect: Rect2 = _screen._tip.get_global_rect()
	print("PROBE_TIP_TOPLEFT rect=", top_rect, " in_screen=",
		top_rect.position.x >= 0.0 and top_rect.position.y >= 0.0
		and top_rect.end.x <= 2400.0 and top_rect.end.y <= 1400.0)
	_screen._on_tip_mode("simple")
	await _frames(2)
	print("PROBE_TIP_LIVE_SWITCH visible=", _screen._tip.visible, " size=", _screen._tip.size,
		" mode=", _screen._tip_mode)
	_screen._hide_tip()
	await _frames(1)
	print("PROBE_TIP_HIDDEN=", _screen._tip.visible)

	for a in _screen._build_actions:
		if str(a.get("name", "")) == "测试流":
			a["del"].pressed.emit()
			break
	await _frames(3)
	print("PROBE_AFTER_DELETE=", HeroBuildStore.get_builds("妲己"))
	print("PROBE_RETURN_BTN=", _screen._return_btn != null and _screen._return_btn.visible,
		" text=", _screen._return_btn.text)

	_restore()
	await _frames(2)
	get_tree().quit()


func _frames(n: int) -> void:
	for i in range(n):

		var f := FileAccess.open("res://saves/hero_builds.json", FileAccess.WRITE)
		if f != null:
			f.store_string(_res_backup)
			f.close()

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

36: 	"孙尚香": SHAPE_SHELL, "沈梦溪": SHAPE_SHELL, "甄姬": SHAPE_WATER,
37: 	"东皇太一": SHAPE_ORB, "吕布": SHAPE_BLADE, "小乔": SHAPE_FAN,
38: 	"安琪拉": SHAPE_FLAME, "妲己": SHAPE_FLAME, "不知火舞": SHAPE_FLAME,
39: 	"马超": SHAPE_SPEAR, "铠": SHAPE_BLADE, "夏侯惇": SHAPE_BLADE, "兰陵王": SHAPE_BLADE,

47: ## 该弹体是否走统一程序化视觉；返回 vkind（0 = 保持旧视觉）。
48: ## 技能弹除「后羿R 太阳箭」外，全部按英雄形状表走统一视觉（安琪拉火球 / 小乔扇面等）。
49: static func vkind_for(bl) -> int:
50: 	if bl == null:
51: 		return 0
52: 	if bool(bl.is_houyi_ult):
53: 		return 0
54: 	var src = bl.source
55: 	if src == null or not is_instance_valid(src):
56: 		return 0
57: 	if not (src is Hero or src is Minion or src is Turret):
58: 		return 0
59: 	if src is Hero and int(bl.skill_id) == 0 and float(src.attack_range) <= 400.0:
60: 		return 0                        # 近战英雄普攻不出弹
61: 	return int(spec_for(bl).get("vk", 0))

64: ## 由弹体推导视觉规格：形状 / 调色板 / 双色 / 尺寸 / 拖尾参数。
65: static func spec_for(bl) -> Dictionary:
66: 	var src = bl.source
67: 	var shape := SHAPE_ORB
68: 	var palette := PALETTE_ALLY if int(bl.team) == 0 else PALETTE_ENEMY
69: 	var is_skill := int(bl.skill_id) != 0
70: 	if src is Turret:
71: 		shape = SHAPE_TOWER
72: 	elif src is Minion:
73: 		var enemy := int(bl.team) != 0
74: 		if str(src.display_name) == "ranged":
75: 			shape = SHAPE_ARROW
76: 			palette = PALETTE_ENEMY_SMALL if enemy else PALETTE_ALLY_SMALL
77: 		elif str(src.display_name) == "siege":
78: 			shape = SHAPE_SIEGE
79: 			palette = PALETTE_ENEMY_SIEGE if enemy else PALETTE_ALLY_SIEGE
80: 	elif src is Hero:
81: 		shape = int(HERO_SHAPE.get(str(src.display_name), SHAPE_ORB))
82: 		var idx := ELEMENT_ORDER.find(str(Vfx.element_of(str(src.display_name))))
83: 		palette = idx if idx >= 0 else 0
84: 
85: 	var cols := colors_for(palette)
86: 	var size_mult := _size_for_palette(palette)
87: 	var trail := _trail_params(shape)
88: 	if is_skill:
89: 		size_mult *= SKILL_SIZE
90: 		trail = [float(trail[0]) * 1.5, float(trail[1]) * 1.4]
91: 	var vk_shape := shape + (SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET if is_skill else 0)
92: 	return {
93: 		"vk": VKIND_BASE + vk_shape * VKIND_SHAPE_MUL + palette,
94: 		"shape": shape,
95: 		"palette": palette,
96: 		"c1": cols[0],
97: 		"c2": cols[1],
98: 		"size_mult": size_mult,
99: 		"trail_size": trail[0],
100: 		"trail_life": trail[1],
101: 	}

104: ## 调色板 → [主色, 亮色]。0-9 = 元素，10-15 = 阵营色（10/12/14 友方，11/13/15 敌方）。
105: static func colors_for(palette: int) -> Array:
106: 	if palette == PALETTE_ALLY or palette == PALETTE_ALLY_SMALL or palette == PALETTE_ALLY_SIEGE:
107: 		return [Color(0.32, 0.82, 1.0), Color(0.85, 0.98, 1.0)]
108: 	if palette == PALETTE_ENEMY or palette == PALETTE_ENEMY_SMALL or palette == PALETTE_ENEMY_SIEGE:
109: 		return [Color(1.0, 0.42, 0.24), Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.55)]
110: 	var key: String = ELEMENT_ORDER[clampi(palette, 0, ELEMENT_ORDER.size() - 1)]
111: 	var d: Dictionary = Vfx.ELEMENTS.get(key, Vfx.ELEMENTS["arcane"])
112: 	return [d["c"], d["c2"]]

116: static func _size_for_palette(palette: int) -> float:
117: 	if palette == PALETTE_ALLY_SMALL or palette == PALETTE_ENEMY_SMALL:
118: 		return 0.8
119: 	if palette == PALETTE_ALLY_SIEGE or palette == PALETTE_ENEMY_SIEGE:
120: 		return 0.95

124: ## 客户端：按 vkind 还原同一形状与尺寸（>SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET 视为技能弹，放大同档）。
125: static func build_from_vkind(vk: int) -> Node3D:
126: 	var t := vk - VKIND_BASE
127: 	var raw_shape: int = t / VKIND_SHAPE_MUL
128: 	var palette: int = t % VKIND_SHAPE_MUL
129: 	var is_skill := raw_shape >= SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET
130: 	var shape := raw_shape - (SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET if is_skill else 0)
131: 	var cols := colors_for(palette)
132: 	var size := _size_for_palette(palette) * (SKILL_SIZE if is_skill else 1.0)
133: 	return build(shape, cols[0], cols[1], size)

137: static func build(shape: int, c1: Color, c2: Color, size_mult: float = 1.0) -> Node3D:
138: 	var root := Node3D.new()
139: 	root.name = "BulletVisual"
140: 	match shape:
141: 		SHAPE_ARROW:
142: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.42), Vector3(0.34, 0.34, 1.0))
143: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.14, 0.14, 0.6))

147: 		SHAPE_SHELL:
148: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.3), Vector3(0.9, 0.9, 0.9))
149: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.42, 0.42, 0.5))
150: 			_add(root, _torus(), _glow(c1, 0.55), Vector3(0.85, 0.85, 0.85), Vector3.ZERO, Vector3(PI * 0.5, 0.0, 0.0))
151: 		SHAPE_CARD:
152: 			_add(root, _quad(), _glow_billboard(c1, 0.85), Vector3(0.6, 0.8, 1.0))
153: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.22, 0.22, 0.22))
154: 		SHAPE_WATER:
155: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.32), Vector3(0.7, 0.8, 1.05))
156: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.3, 0.4, 0.6))
157: 		SHAPE_BLADE:
158: 			_add(root, _quad(), _glow_billboard(c1, 0.9), Vector3(1.2, 0.22, 1.0))
159: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.18, 0.18, 0.3))
160: 		SHAPE_TOWER:
161: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.3), Vector3(0.95, 0.95, 0.95))
162: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.44, 0.44, 0.44))
163: 		SHAPE_SIEGE:
164: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.28), Vector3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0))
165: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
166: 			_add(root, _torus(), _glow(c1, 0.4), Vector3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), Vector3.ZERO, Vector3(PI * 0.5, 0.0, 0.0))
167: 		SHAPE_FAN:
168: 			# 回旋扇面：扇叶（扇形面）+ 加色描边 + 扇骨 + 轴心；整片绕竖轴自转
169: 			var spin := Node3D.new()
170: 			spin.name = "Spin"
171: 			root.add_child(spin)
172: 			_add(spin, _fan_mesh(), _fan_mat(c2), Vector3.ONE)
173: 			_add(spin, _fan_mesh(), _glow(c1, 0.5), Vector3.ONE * 1.06)
174: 			for i in range(3):
175: 				var a := deg_to_rad(-42.0 + 42.0 * float(i))
176: 				var p := Vector3(sin(a) * 0.46, 0.015, cos(a) * 0.46)
177: 				_add(spin, _quad(), _glow(c2, 0.9), Vector3(0.045, 0.52, 1.0), p, Vector3(-PI * 0.5, a, 0.0))
178: 			_add(spin, _sphere(), _core(c1), Vector3(0.19, 0.19, 0.19))
179: 			root.set_meta("spin", 5.0)
180: 		SHAPE_FLAME:
181: 			# 火焰弹：亮核 + 外层火色光晕 + 3 片舌状火苗（随机偏转，避免死板）
182: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.42), Vector3(1.05, 1.05, 1.3))
183: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.46, 0.46, 0.58))
184: 			for i in range(3):
185: 				_add(root, _quad(), _glow_billboard(c1, 0.55), Vector3(0.5, 0.85, 1.0),
186: 					Vector3(0.0, 0.06, -0.22 - 0.1 * float(i)), Vector3(0.0, 0.0, randf() * TAU))
187: 		SHAPE_SPEAR:
188: 			# 枪芒：细长光柱 + 枪尖锥 + 亮核
189: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.55), Vector3(0.32, 0.32, 1.9))
190: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.11, 0.11, 1.35))
191: 			_add(root, _cone(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.26, 0.55, 0.26), Vector3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), Vector3(PI * 0.5, 0.0, 0.0))
192: 		_:  # SHAPE_ORB
193: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _glow(c1, 0.32), Vector3(0.95, 0.95, 0.95))
194: 			_add(root, _sphere(), _core(c2), Vector3(0.34, 0.34, 0.34))
195: 			_add(root, _torus(), _glow(c1, 0.55), Vector3(0.9, 0.9, 0.9), Vector3.ZERO, Vector3(PI * 0.5, 0.0, 0.0))
196: 	root.scale = Vector3.ONE * size_mult

235: ## 扇面：扇形三角面（半角 65°，半径 1.0，平铺在 XZ 平面，绕原点展开）
236: static func _fan_mesh() -> Mesh:
237: 	if _mesh_cache.has("fan"):
238: 		return _mesh_cache["fan"]
239: 	var seg := 14
240: 	var half := deg_to_rad(65.0)
241: 	var verts := PackedVector3Array()
242: 	var idx := PackedInt32Array()
243: 	verts.append(Vector3.ZERO)
244: 	for i in range(seg + 1):
245: 		var a := -half + 2.0 * half * float(i) / float(seg)
246: 		verts.append(Vector3(sin(a), 0.0, cos(a)))
247: 	for i in range(seg):
248: 		idx.append(0)
249: 		idx.append(i + 1)
250: 		idx.append(i + 2)
251: 	var arr := []
252: 	arr.resize(Mesh.ARRAY_MAX)
253: 	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = verts
254: 	arr[Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX] = idx
255: 	var m := ArrayMesh.new()
256: 	m.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, arr)
257: 	_mesh_cache["fan"] = m
258: 	return m

266: 	m.bottom_radius = 0.5
267: 	m.height = 1.0
268: 	m.radial_segments = 8

274: ## 扇面材质：半透明自发光（双面，贴图无光照也能看清轮廓）
275: static func _fan_mat(c: Color) -> StandardMaterial3D:
276: 	var key := "f" + c.to_html()
277: 	if _mat_cache.has(key):
278: 		return _mat_cache[key]
279: 	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
280: 	m.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
281: 	m.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
282: 	m.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_DISABLED
283: 	m.disable_receive_shadows = true
284: 	m.albedo_color = Color(c.r, c.g, c.b, 0.88)
285: 	m.emission_enabled = true
286: 	m.emission = c
287: 	m.emission_energy_multiplier = 0.8
288: 	_mat_cache[key] = m
289: 	return m

292: static func _glow(c: Color, alpha: float) -> StandardMaterial3D:
293: 	var key := "g%s%.2f" % [c.to_html(), alpha]
294: 	if _mat_cache.has(key):
295: 		return _mat_cache[key]
296: 	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
297: 	m.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
298: 	m.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
299: 	m.blend_mode = BaseMaterial3D.BLEND_MODE_ADD
300: 	m.depth_draw_mode = BaseMaterial3D.DEPTH_DRAW_DISABLED
301: 	m.cull_mode = BaseMaterial3D.CULL_DISABLED
302: 	m.disable_receive_shadows = true
303: 	m.albedo_color = Color(c.r, c.g, c.b, alpha)
304: 	_mat_cache[key] = m
305: 	return m
306: 
307: 
308: static func _glow_billboard(c: Color, alpha: float) -> StandardMaterial3D:
309: 	var key := "b%s%.2f" % [c.to_html(), alpha]
310: 	if _mat_cache.has(key):
311: 		return _mat_cache[key]
312: 	var m := _glow(c, alpha).duplicate() as StandardMaterial3D
313: 	m.billboard_mode = BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED
314: 	_mat_cache[key] = m
315: 	return m
316: 
317: 
318: static func _core(c: Color) -> StandardMaterial3D:
319: 	var key := "c" + c.to_html()
320: 	if _mat_cache.has(key):
321: 		return _mat_cache[key]
322: 	var m := StandardMaterial3D.new()
323: 	m.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
324: 	m.albedo_color = Color(minf(1.0, c.r + 0.15), minf(1.0, c.g + 0.15), minf(1.0, c.b + 0.15), 1.0)
325: 	m.emission_enabled = true
326: 	m.emission = c
327: 	m.emission_energy_multiplier = 0.6
328: 	m.disable_receive_shadows = true
329: 	_mat_cache[key] = m
330: 	return m

333: static func _add(root: Node3D, mesh: Mesh, mat: Material, scl: Vector3,
334: 		pos: Vector3 = Vector3.ZERO, rot: Vector3 = Vector3.ZERO) -> MeshInstance3D:
335: 	var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
336: 	mi.mesh = mesh
337: 	mi.material_override = mat
338: 	mi.scale = scl
339: 	mi.position = pos
340: 	mi.rotation = rot
341: 	mi.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
342: 	root.add_child(mi)
343: 	return mi

353: 		SHAPE_BLADE: return [0.18, 0.26]
354: 		SHAPE_TOWER: return [0.18, 0.26]
355: 		SHAPE_SIEGE: return [0.24, 0.34]
356: 		SHAPE_FAN: return [0.3, 0.46]

```
## 解码 vkind（与 spec_for 对称）：shape / palette / slot（-1=普攻）/ is_skill / size
static func decode_vkind(vk: int) -> Dictionary:
	var t := vk - VKIND_BASE
	var raw_shape: int = t / VKIND_SHAPE_MUL
	var palette: int = t % VKIND_SHAPE_MUL
	var shape := raw_shape
	var slot := -1
	var size := _size_for_palette(palette)
	if raw_shape >= SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET:
		var code := raw_shape - SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET
		slot = clampi(code / SKILL_SLOT_STRIDE, 0, SKILL_SLOT_COUNT - 1)
		shape = code % SKILL_SLOT_STRIDE + 1
		size *= SKILL_SIZE * (SKILL_ULT_SIZE if slot >= 2 else 1.0)
	return {"shape": shape, "palette": palette, "slot": slot, "is_skill": slot >= 0, "size": size}

static func build_from_vkind(vk: int) -> Node3D:
	var d := decode_vkind(vk)
	var cols := colors_for(int(d["palette"]))
	return build(int(d["shape"]), cols[0], cols[1], float(d["size"]))
```

## 解码 vkind（与 spec_for 对称）：shape / palette / slot（-1=普攻）/ is_skill / size
static func decode_vkind(vk: int) -> Dictionary:
	var t := vk - VKIND_BASE
	var raw_shape: int = t / VKIND_SHAPE_MUL
	var palette: int = t % VKIND_SHAPE_MUL
	var shape := raw_shape
	var slot := -1
	var size := _size_for_palette(palette)
	if raw_shape >= SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET:
		var code := raw_shape - SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET
		slot = clampi(code / SKILL_SLOT_STRIDE, 0, SKILL_SLOT_COUNT - 1)
		shape = code % SKILL_SLOT_STRIDE + 1
		size *= SKILL_SIZE * (SKILL_ULT_SIZE if slot >= 2 else 1.0)
	return {"shape": shape, "palette": palette, "slot": slot, "is_skill": slot >= 0, "size": size}

static func build_from_vkind(vk: int) -> Node3D:

	var cols := colors_for(int(d["palette"]))

Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

func _sig(n: Node) -> String:
	var parts: Array = []

			parts.append("%s|%.2f,%.2f,%.2f|%.2f,%.2f,%.2f" % [mi.mesh.get_class() if mi.mesh else "null", mi.scale.x, mi.scale.y, mi.scale.z, mi.position.x, mi.position.y, mi.position.z])

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, message, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.name: web_search

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

## Primary Request and Intent
- Acting as teammate `ui-skin-secondary` under Lead `lead`, working in HonorKing repo `C:\Users\18749\Documents\honor-king` (Godot 4.7.2, GDScript, no git, minimal changes).
- Prior tasks completed earlier (background, no action needed): task-8 UI skin unification; task-16 created `scripts/ui/LoadoutScreen.gd` + `scenes/loadout.tscn` (Lead verified/online); task-19 added hover tooltip (simple/detail) + slot drag reorder to `LoadoutScreen.gd` — completed at revision 3, report sent.
- **Current task (task-28, claimed at revision 1 → now in_progress revision 2)**: Lead message: "开工：共享任务 task-28「P0-3 技能弹道按槽位分形状」。请先 team_task_get → claim（expected_revision=1），按描述改 `scripts/core/BulletVisual.gd`（必要时 `scripts/entities/Bullet.gd`），让同英雄 Q/W/R 三发技能弹形状互不相同（大招更大更长拖尾），vkind 编码与解码对称、普攻弹不变、纯视觉不改伤害。别碰 NetSession/Hero.gd/SpellFxTable.gd。验收：headless editor 无 Parse Error；探针打印三发弹 vkind 与还原形状并断言不同。完成后 complete + send_message 报告 revision、编码公式、断言结果。"
- task-28 spec details: only modify `scripts/core/BulletVisual.gd` (optionally `scripts/entities/Bullet.gd` to pass slot); do NOT touch NetSession/Hero.gd/SpellFxTable.gd. Current `vkind_for`/`spec_for` gives same base shape to all skill bullets (`shape + SKILL_SHAPE_OFFSET(20)`, size ×1.45); `build_from_vkind` decodes client-side. Requirements: (1) backward-compatible encoding, no conflict with palette encoding, `vkind_for` and `build_from_vkind` fully symmetric, design explicit formula e.g. `vkind = shape_base + slot*STEP + (20 if is_skill) + palette*PALETTE_STRIDE`, read file first to confirm existing vkind structure; (2) normal attack (`skill_id==0`) unchanged; (3) skill bullets slot0/1/2 each different shape (choose from 球/箭/炮/飞剑/冰锥/法球, may add 1-2 low-poly mesh shape funcs), slot2 = 1.45 × 1.25, longer trail; (4) if `Bullet.gd` lacks slot info, derive from `skill_id` after reading code to confirm semantics; (5) visuals only, no damage/hit changes. Acceptance: `--headless --editor --quit` no Parse Error; probe spawns hero Q/W/R skill bullets, prints `vkind` + `build_from_vkind` restored shape, asserts all different; confirm normal-attack vkind matches old formula. Report revision, encoding formula, assertion results; complete task + send_message.
